title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A licensed user of the Flock camera system and of other police databases is accused of running searches for personal reasons rather than for police work. The systems performed as designed: they returned location and record information to someone holding valid credentials. The failure sits at the point of use, not at the point of the model or the match.

The searches are alleged to have happened repeatedly across 2024 and 2025, which is the pattern that audit trails exist to surface. Catching this would have required routine review of query logs against case numbers or stated purposes, and a process for flagging searches that name no active investigation. The department's own internal affairs investigation, which took four weeks, is the check that eventually ran, and it ran only after the woman came forward.

What is not established is whether Rogers is guilty of any crime. A criminal complaint is an accusation, an internal affairs finding is an administrative conclusion, and a restraining order is a protective order rather than a verdict. The Select Board has not yet voted on his employment.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the relationship about five years ago, changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits after leaving. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 for possible state law violations. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, the department found he had used state systems to obtain information about the woman. Rogers was placed on paid administrative leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order against him lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing is scheduled next week, when town leaders could vote on his employment status.
